description: An introduction to the meaning, functions, levels and resources of business management, including managerial skills, leadership, decision-making, business departments and the challenges of managing a business in Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: What is the best meaning of business management?

options.text: The buying and selling of goods only
The process of planning, organising, directing and controlling resources to achieve business goals
The keeping of business records and accounts
The payment of taxes to the government

mcq.explanation: Management is the process of coordinating human, financial, physical and information resources through planning, organising, directing and controlling so that the goals of the business are achieved.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic functions of management?
mcq.explanation: The main functions of management are planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling. Advertising is a marketing activity, not a core management function.

mcq.questionText: The management function that involves setting goals and deciding in advance what to do, how and when to do it is called:
mcq.explanation: Planning is the first function of management; it involves looking ahead, setting objectives and choosing the course of action to reach those objectives.

mcq.questionText: Recruiting, selecting, training and placing employees in a business is part of which management function?
mcq.explanation: Staffing deals with filling the positions in the organisation with the right people through recruitment, selection, training and placement.

mcq.questionText: At which level of management are the managing director and chief executive officer found?
mcq.explanation: Top-level management (e.g. managing director, CEO, board of directors) sets overall objectives and policies and is responsible for the whole organisation.

mcq.questionText: Foremen and supervisors who deal directly with workers belong to which level of management?
mcq.explanation: Lower or supervisory management consists of supervisors and foremen who directly oversee the operative workers and ensure daily tasks are carried out.

mcq.questionText: The 4 Ms of management resources stand for:
mcq.explanation: The resources managed in a business are commonly grouped as the 4 Ms: Men (human resources), Money (finance), Materials (physical resources) and Machines.

mcq.questionText: According to management skills, the ability to think and understand the business as a whole is called:
mcq.explanation: Conceptual skill is the ability to see the organisation as a whole and understand how its parts relate; it is most important at top levels of management.

mcq.questionText: Which skill is MOST important for lower-level managers such as workshop supervisors?
mcq.explanation: Technical skill, the knowledge of specific methods and procedures, is most needed at the supervisory level because these managers directly guide workers doing the task.

mcq.questionText: The main difference between management and administration is that administration mainly deals with:

options.text: Supervising the workers on the shop floor

mcq.explanation: Administration is concerned with the formulation of broad policies and objectives, while management is concerned with carrying out those policies to achieve the goals.

mcq.questionText: The function that ensures all departments and activities work together in harmony is called:
mcq.explanation: Coordination is the process of harmonising the efforts of different individuals and departments so that they work together towards common goals.

mcq.questionText: Dividing work into small tasks so that each worker performs a specific task is known as:
mcq.explanation: Division of labour means splitting work into separate tasks, and specialisation means workers concentrate on the task they do best, which raises efficiency and output.

mcq.questionText: Which department of a business is responsible for recruiting, training and the welfare of employees?
mcq.explanation: The human resources (personnel) department handles recruitment, training, motivation, payment and general welfare of the workers in a business.

mcq.questionText: The management function that measures actual performance against the plan and corrects deviations is called:
mcq.explanation: Controlling involves comparing actual results with the set standards or plans and taking corrective action where there are differences.

mcq.questionText: Giving workers a bonus or higher pay in order to make them work harder is an example of:
mcq.explanation: Incentives such as bonuses, allowances and promotion are used to motivate workers, encouraging them to put in more effort towards the goals of the business.

fib.questionText: The process of getting work done through people by planning, organising, directing and controlling resources is called _____.
fib.explanation: Management is the coordination of resources and people to achieve the objectives of an organisation.

fib.questionText: The first function of management, which involves deciding in advance what to do, is _____.
fib.explanation: Planning sets the objectives and the means of achieving them before any other function is performed.

fib.questionText: Arranging resources and grouping activities into departments so that work can be done is the function of _____.
fib.explanation: Organising creates the structure of the business by grouping tasks, assigning duties and establishing relationships of authority.

fib.questionText: The level of management that sets overall policies and objectives for the whole business is the _____ level.
fib.explanation: Top-level management, such as the board of directors and managing director, is responsible for major decisions and overall direction.

fib.questionText: Supervisors and foremen who control daily work of operatives belong to the _____ level of management.
fib.explanation: The lower or supervisory level directly oversees the workers carrying out the day-to-day tasks.

fib.questionText: In the 4 Ms of management, the resource 'Money' refers to the _____ resources of the business.
fib.explanation: Money represents the financial resources (capital and funds) needed to run and grow the business.

fib.questionText: The managerial skill that involves the ability to work well with and through other people is called _____ skill.
fib.explanation: Human (interpersonal) skill is the ability to communicate, motivate and lead people effectively and is important at all levels.

fib.questionText: Splitting a job into small tasks where each worker does one task is called division of _____.
fib.explanation: Division of labour increases efficiency because workers become skilled and faster at the specific task they repeat.

fib.questionText: The department responsible for producing or manufacturing the goods of a business is the _____ department.
fib.explanation: The production department converts raw materials into finished goods ready for sale.

fib.questionText: Choosing the best course of action from among several alternatives is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Decision-making is at the heart of management; managers must select the best alternative to solve problems and reach goals.

tf.questionText: Management is the process of achieving business goals through the efficient use of resources.
tf.explanation: Management aims to achieve objectives by using human, financial, physical and information resources efficiently and effectively.

tf.questionText: Planning is done only after the work has already been completed.
tf.explanation: Planning is done in advance, before the work begins; it decides what is to be done and how.

tf.questionText: Staffing involves recruiting, selecting and training the people needed by the business.
tf.explanation: Staffing is the function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation with suitable people.

tf.questionText: The managing director belongs to the lower (supervisory) level of management.
tf.explanation: The managing director is part of top-level management, not the supervisory level.

tf.questionText: Conceptual skill is more important for top managers than for lower-level supervisors.
tf.explanation: Top managers need conceptual skill to see the whole organisation and make broad decisions, while supervisors rely more on technical skill.

tf.questionText: In the 4 Ms, 'Materials' refers to the physical resources such as raw materials and stock.
tf.explanation: Materials are the physical inputs such as raw materials, components and stock used in production.

tf.questionText: Administration is generally concerned with carrying out daily operative tasks rather than setting policy.
tf.explanation: Administration is mainly concerned with formulating policies and objectives; management carries them out through daily operations.

tf.questionText: Division of labour can increase the efficiency and output of workers.
tf.explanation: When workers specialise in one task they become more skilled and faster, raising overall output and efficiency.

tf.questionText: Controlling means comparing actual performance with plans and taking corrective action.
tf.explanation: Controlling checks whether results match the standards set and corrects any deviations.

tf.questionText: Motivation has no effect on how hard employees work in a business.
tf.explanation: Motivation, through incentives like bonuses and good working conditions, strongly affects how hard and how well employees work.

summary.correctAnswer: Business management is the process of planning, organising, staffing, directing/leading and controlling the resources of a business so as to achieve its goals efficiently and effectively.
summary.explanation: This definition captures management as both a process and the coordination of resources towards set objectives.

summary.questionText: List the main functions of management.
summary.correctAnswer: The main functions of management are planning, organising, staffing, directing (leading), coordinating and controlling.
summary.explanation: These functions describe what managers do at every level to run an organisation successfully.

summary.questionText: State the three levels of management.
summary.correctAnswer: The three levels of management are top-level management, middle-level management and lower (supervisory) level management.
summary.explanation: Each level has different responsibilities, from setting overall policy at the top to supervising daily work at the bottom.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of top-level management.
summary.correctAnswer: Top-level management, such as the board of directors and managing director, sets the overall objectives and policies of the business, makes major decisions and is responsible for the success of the whole organisation.
summary.explanation: Top managers give the business its overall direction and accountability.

summary.questionText: Identify the 4 Ms of management resources and what each stands for.
summary.correctAnswer: The 4 Ms are Men (human resources/workers), Money (financial resources/capital), Materials (physical resources such as raw materials and stock) and Machines (equipment used in production).
summary.explanation: Managers must combine these four resources well to produce goods and services and reach business goals.

summary.questionText: Describe the three skills of a good manager.
summary.correctAnswer: A good manager needs technical skill (knowledge of methods and procedures), human skill (ability to work with and lead people) and conceptual skill (ability to understand and plan for the business as a whole).
summary.explanation: These three skills are needed in different proportions at different levels of management.

summary.correctAnswer: Administration is concerned with determining broad policies and objectives of the business, while management is concerned with carrying out those policies and getting the work done through people to achieve the objectives.
summary.explanation: Administration is the thinking/policy function and management is the doing/executing function.

summary.questionText: Explain the benefits of division of labour and specialisation.
summary.correctAnswer: Division of labour and specialisation increase efficiency and output, raise the skill and speed of workers, save time, reduce wastage and improve the quality of goods produced.
summary.explanation: By repeating one task, workers become experts at it, which improves productivity in the business.

summary.questionText: Name the main departments (functions) found in a business.
summary.correctAnswer: The main departments are production, marketing (sales), finance (accounts), human resources (personnel) and purchasing (procurement).
summary.explanation: Each department handles a specialised function but they must be coordinated to achieve the goals of the business.

summary.questionText: State four challenges faced in managing a business in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Challenges include shortage of capital/finance, lack of skilled and motivated workers, strong competition, changes in government policy and taxes, poor infrastructure such as unreliable power, and changing customer demand.
summary.explanation: These challenges can lower efficiency and profits, so managers must plan and adapt to overcome them.

hoq.questionText: A bakery in Mwanza is failing to deliver bread on time because the production, sales and delivery sections each work without consulting one another. Which management function is MOST lacking?
hoq.explanation: When departments do not work together in harmony, the function of coordination is missing; coordination harmonises the efforts of all sections towards the common goal of timely delivery.

hoq.questionText: The owner of a growing hardware shop in Dar es Salaam spends all her time personally serving every customer and keeping every record, so the shop cannot expand. What management principle should she apply to solve this?

options.text: Apply division of labour by hiring and assigning duties to staff
Lower the prices of all goods

hoq.explanation: By dividing the work and assigning specific duties to employees (division of labour and delegation), the owner frees herself to plan and manage, allowing the business to grow.

hoq.questionText: A factory manager notices that monthly output is far below the target set at the start of the year, so he investigates the causes and adjusts the work schedule. He is mainly carrying out which management function, and at which point in the management process?

options.text: Planning, at the start of the process
Staffing, in the middle of the process
Controlling, by comparing results with the plan and taking corrective action
Organising, by grouping activities into departments

hoq.explanation: Comparing actual output against the target and then taking corrective action is the controlling function, which closes the management cycle by ensuring plans are achieved.
